SL-000002.transcript:
Member (Chantal Roy): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Chantal Roy, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Roy): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Roy): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Chantal Roy): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Chantal Roy): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Chantal Roy): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Chantal Roy): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Chantal Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Chantal Roy): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Chantal Roy): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Chantal Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000020.transcript:
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Gurpreet Wilson, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): How old is he?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Fourteen.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Great, that helps.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Fortin): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Emma Fortin, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Fortin): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Fortin): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Emma Fortin): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Emma Fortin): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Emma Fortin): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Emma Fortin): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Emma Fortin): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Emma Fortin): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Emma Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Morrison): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Noah Morrison, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Morrison): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Noah Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Noah Morrison): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Noah Morrison): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Noah Morrison): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Member (Noah Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Noah Morrison): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Noah Morrison): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Noah Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Wilson): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Hannah Wilson, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.

Member (Noah Chen): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Noah Chen, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.

Member (Noah Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam Cote): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Liam Cote, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Cote): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Liam Cote): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): How old is he?
Member (Liam Cote): Fourteen.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Liam Cote): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Liam Cote): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Liam Cote): Yes, here in town.

Member (Liam Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Liam Cote): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Liam Cote): That's disappointing.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Liam Cote): How would I check that?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Liam Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Owen Lavoie): I was approved for this weeks ago and I still haven't been reimbursed.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Owen Lavoie, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Lavoie): It was a massage therapy claim for 120 dollars.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Owen Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The payment went to your old bank account and was returned. I've updated your direct deposit and reissued it, so it'll arrive within three business days.
Member (Owen Lavoie): So I'll get it this time?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Yes. I've updated the account and reissued the payment, so it should land within three business days.
Member (Owen Lavoie): Is there anything else going to the old account?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No, all future claims will go to the new one.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the new account is on file and the 120-dollar payment is reissued. You'll see it within three business days.
Member (Owen Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000813.transcript:
Member (Fatima O'Brien): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Fatima O'Brien, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima O'Brien): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Fatima O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Fatima O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Fatima O'Brien): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Fatima O'Brien): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Fatima O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Fatima O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Fatima O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Fatima O'Brien): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

SL-000820.transcript:
Member (Fatima Morrison): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Fatima Morrison, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Morrison): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Fatima Morrison): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Fatima Morrison): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Fatima Morrison): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Fatima Morrison): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Fatima Morrison): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Fatima Morrison): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Fatima Morrison): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the crown is approved, and your dentist will get the confirmation today with your co-payment.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Morrison): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Owen Morrison, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Morrison): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Morrison): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): When did you go off work?
Member (Owen Morrison): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Owen Morrison): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Owen Morrison): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Member (Owen Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Owen Morrison): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Owen Morrison): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Owen Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Wilson): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Mei Wilson, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Wilson): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Wilson): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mei Wilson): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Mei Wilson): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Mei Wilson): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Mei Wilson): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Mei Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Mei Wilson): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Mei Wilson): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Mei Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: a payment trace is open, it can take up to ten business days, and you'll get a call when it's done.

Member (Fatima Chen): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Fatima Chen, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Chen): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?

Member (Fatima Chen): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Fatima Chen): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has the dental office called us about this directly?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Are you in any pain right now?

Member (Fatima Chen): So is this actually getting fixed today?

Member (Fatima Chen): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Fatima Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-001170.transcript:
Member (Fatima Lavoie): My pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Fatima Lavoie, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Where is the money going?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Who follows up?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Fatima Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Arjun Ahmed, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): My spouse has coverage through her work too.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Arjun Ahmed): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): How old is he?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Fourteen.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?

SL-001486.transcript:
Member (Liam Chen): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Liam Chen, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Chen): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Chen): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Liam Chen): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Liam Chen): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Liam Chen): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Liam Chen): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Liam Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Liam Chen): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Liam Chen): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Liam Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Gurpreet Singh): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Gurpreet Singh, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Singh): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Singh): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Gurpreet Singh): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Gurpreet Singh): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Gurpreet Singh): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Gurpreet Singh): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Gurpreet Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Gurpreet Singh): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Gurpreet Singh): Great, that helps.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Gurpreet Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Owen Ahmed, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.

Member (Tyler Morrison): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Tyler Morrison, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.

Member (Tyler Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Tyler Morrison): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Tyler Morrison): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Tyler Morrison): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Tyler Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Tyler Morrison): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Tyler Morrison): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Tyler Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mei Ahmed): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mei Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Olivia Wilson): I'm following up again — my dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Olivia Wilson, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Wilson): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Olivia Wilson): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Olivia Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Olivia Wilson): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Olivia Wilson): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Olivia Wilson): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Olivia Wilson): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Olivia Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Olivia Wilson): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Olivia Wilson): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Olivia Wilson): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
